finding_key: .github/workflows/agent-iterate-ci.yml::$github_output heredoc uses a fixed, guessable delimiter around attacker-influenceable text (output injection)
evidence: The step at agent-iterate-ci.yml ("Summarize the failure") does write `summary<<HARNESS_EOF` / script stdout / `HARNESS_EOF` into $GITHUB_OUTPUT with a fixed, guessable delimiter, and the stdout embeds report-derived strings (`detail.failureSummary`, `lane.lane`) parsed from the downloaded `harness-reports` artifact, which is produced by branch code (scripts/verify-self.mjs runs from the PR branch in CI). So a crafted/modified report can emit a bare `HARNESS_EOF` at column 0 and then re-assign `summary=` or other outputs — the classic GitHub "use a random delimiter" issue; the claim's mechanism is technically correct. One nuance the claim glosses over: as the repo's own producer is written, extractFailureSummary (verify-self.mjs) returns a single `split("\n")` line truncated to 500 chars, so under the honest path no newline can appear — exploitation requires the branch to alter verify-self.mjs or the artifact, i.e. it presumes an untrusted branch. Marginal impact is small because that same job already checks out the branch, runs `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` (lifecycle scripts) and gives the agent Bash with the App token in scope, so a branch-controlling attacker already has execution there; and the failureSummary text reaches the prompt anyway. Real but hardening-grade.
